collection: National Museum of Women in the Arts

materials.content:
Charcoal on medium thick, cream, moderately textured laid paper; Watermark: Blind stamp at corner, STRATHMORE with thistle
(Source: Paper Survey researched by Judith C. Walsh and published in Lynes, 1999.)

cr_data.provenance:
Donated in 1986 to the National Museum of Women in the Arts by its founder, Wilhelmina Cole Holladay. 
(Source: National Museum of Women in the Arts, 2025)
remarks_1999: On verso is burnished image of a lost charcoal drawing that closely resembles cat. no. 336. Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_post_1999: When the NMWA received the drawing was dated 1923, but NMWA’s files now indicate date made as 1921. Lynes publication dates work as 1920/1921. (Source: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by National Museum of Women in the Arts (NMWA), 2025)

credit_line: National Museum of Women in the Arts, Washington, D.C.; Gift of Wallace and Wilhelmina Holladay
description: Six dark gray avocados sit in a black basket, which casts a black shadow. The avocadoes shine, reflecting an unseen light source. The objects contrast with the plain white background.
imageCaption: Image courtesy of a scanned transparency made for Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. This image has not been color proofed and may differ from the original. It will be replaced when newer photography becomes available.
